To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

MON87460 maize event, which is a biotechnology-derived drought tolerant maize, increased grain yield by increasing ear growth during siliking under water limited (drought) conditions, which was associated with decreased leaf area, lower sap flow rate, and higher soil moisture content at 0-5 cm soil depth.
MON 8746O increased yield under water-limited conditions by reducing leaf growth, which resulted in lower stress and increased grain yield.

a biotechnology-derived drought tolerant maize event, MON 87460 (expressing CspB), increased grain yield under water limited conditions compared to a conventional control by increasing ear growth, which subsequently resulted in increased kernel number and yield.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the physiological responses of a biotechnology-derived drought tolerant maize to drought.
the whole plant physiological mechanisms that underlie increased grain yield in MON 874602 under drought conditions.
whole-plant physiological responses related to increased yield in MON 8746, and these responses were consistent in three field trials.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

MON 8746 increased grain yield under WL conditions by decreasing leaf area and growth, and consequently water use, during silking, and this was associated with increased ear growth, which increased kernel number and yield.
MON 8746 increased yield under drought conditions by decreasing water loss during grain fill, thereby increasing the amount of water available to the developing grain.

MON 8746O plants acclimated better to water-limited conditions by lowering the leaf growth and consequently decreasing water use during the silking period, which subsequently resulted in increased ear development and kernel number, and ultimately increased yield under drought conditions.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
MON 874601 is a drought-tolerant event that has improved grain yield by increasing kernel number and harvest under drought stress.
MON 874601 increased grain yield under WL conditions by acclimation to drought stress during silking, and that the physiological responses in MON87460 were consistent across years and sites.

MON 87406 acclimated better to water-limited conditions by lowering leaf growth during silking and thereby decreased water use during this critical period, which increased the ear growth and grain yield.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a biotechnology-derived drought tolerance trait can improve grain yield by increasing kernel number and harvest Index under drought conditions.
MON 8746 increased yield under water-limited conditions by increasing the kernel number, which is a key determinant of grain yield.
the CspB protein in MON 87406 is not the only factor that is responsible for drought tolerance in this event.
